reasoning: Interval cost depends on N and N' only -- D = (N/2+1)^3 is independent of L -- so moving the box to L* is FREE in compute terms and is the single cheapest available width improvement. At N=64/N'=80 the width falls from 4.763e-4 (published, L=20) to 2.236e-4 at L=14 for H2+, a 2.13x tightening at identical cost and memory. The L=12/N=48/N'=64 cell reaches 4.716e-4, i.e. it MATCHES the published width with D_aux=35937 instead of 68921, so if the goal is to reproduce rather than improve, the certified run gets ~9x cheaper. The separator is not the binding constraint: varying rho over the full 0-4x allowance range moves LG by at most 3.0e-05 across the six recommended cells (1.8e-05 at the top one), so the certified phase can use a coarse (cheap) mu2 separator. Priority for the small number of affordable interval runs: (1) H2+ L=14 N=64 as the headline improvement, (2) H3^2+ d=4 L=12 N=64 as the second system, (3) H2+ L=12 N=48 as the cost-reduction demonstration.

blockers.severity: blocks the d_paper=2.8 decomposition and any agreement claim
blockers.statement: For linear H3^2+ at d_paper=2.8 the float two-sided chain places lambda_1 ABOVE the supplied reference -0.936459672195 (h3plus_reference.json reference_value.secondary, stated as a variational UPPER bound with error 5e-8). At L=12,N=64,N'=80 the enclosure is [-0.9364012453, -0.9363042805], which EXCLUDES the reference by 5.8427e-05 -- a factor 1168.5 over the stated 5e-8 error bar. 12 of 14 d=2.8 LG cells show the same sign.
what_was_ruled_out: 3-centre assembly (matches the independent interval assembler step3_checks.json to 3.1e-13 at this very geometry)
LG implementation (reproduces the published certified H2+ A0, A2 and both separator variants inside their recorded intervals)
separator validity (rho <= min(eee2, oee, eoe) with a 6.2e-3 margin; pushing rho down 20x moves LG by only 1.3e-5, still above the reference)
confinement hypothesis (sigma = -0.304 > lambda_1 at L=12, margin 0.63)
geometry mismatch (V_nn_std = 1.7857142857 in the artifact confirms adjacent spacing 1.4 std = 2.8 paper, matching the centres used)
blockers.pattern: Smallest (lambda_ref - LG_lower) over all LG cells of a system: +7.571e-05 for H2+ (at L=14 N=64, EXACT spheroidal reference), +4.618e-06 for H3^2+ d=4 (at L=20 N=64, Gaussian reference), -1.084e-03 for H3^2+ d=2.8 (at L=20 N=32, Gaussian reference). Only the Gaussian-referenced systems are tight or negative, and d=4 is not comfortable either: its margin is down to 4.6e-6, so a further bias of that size in the same direction would put d=4 in conflict too. The d=4 reference should therefore not be relied on below ~1e-5 despite its quoted 1.5e-7.
blockers.consequence: the H3^2+ Gaussian value cannot serve as an independent cross-check at the 5e-8 level it claims. For d=2.8 it cannot be used at all. W and L*(N) are reference-INDEPENDENT and remain valid for all three systems; only truncation_term and LG_discretisation_term are affected (they are reported but must not be used for d=2.8).
blockers.recommended_next_step: recompute the H3^2+ floating-Gaussian reference at both geometries with a convergence ladder carried until successive decrements fall below 1e-8, and check it against the spectral LOWER bound, which is the constraint that actually excludes the present value: at d=2.8, L=12, N=64, N'=80 the Lehmann-Goerisch bound gives lambda_1 >= -0.9364012453, so any reference more negative than that is too low. (The Dirichlet Ritz value is an UPPER bound, lambda_1 <= -0.9363103469 at L=10 N=64, and is consistent with the present reference -- it is not the binding constraint.)
blockers.separator_ruled_out_quantitatively: In every one of the 36 cells where a three-N extrapolation of mu2 is available (geometric extrapolation of the oee Ritz decrements over N = 32/48/64), rho lies below the extrapolated true mu2 by 1.85e-03 to 6.20e-03. That includes all 10 violating d=2.8 cells it covers, and no cell anywhere has an unsafe separator, so no violation can be attributed to the separator.
